analytic.title: Islamic exegetical terms in Yefet ben ʿEli’s commentaries on the Holy Scriptures

biblStruct.note: Following the Qur̓anic assertion concerning its own content Islamic exegesis differentiates between muḥkam and mutashābih verses, as two kinds of formulation of God’s word. Although there are discrepancies between Muslim scholars concerning the meaning of these crucial terms, they are usually perceived as antonyms. Therefore, it is possible to assert that they refer to clear and ambiguous formulations. It has been suggested that the tenth–eleventh-century Karaite exegete Yefet ben ̔Eli was generally influenced by Muslim exegesis and that he adopted its terminology in that he used the same set of terms to describe similar scriptural phenomena. This article advances a hypothesis that irrespectively of Yefet’s general adoption of the Islamic hermeneutic distinction between two kinds of divine utterances – clear and ambiguous – he defines them differently as ‘precise’ or ‘specific’ and ‘imprecise’, ‘unspecified’ or ‘indeterminate’ sayings. Furthermore, he calls the second type of utterance by a different Arabic term (mursal).
